newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 17.

text.p: Tenet Healthcare is expected to announce Thursday an agreement to acquire OrNda Healthcorp for $1.82 billion in stock, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.
- Norfolk Southern Corp might seek railway tracks or some other concession in exchange for not opposing CSX Corp's purchase of Conrail Inc.
- France sold Thomson SA to the country's Lagardere Groupe and South Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co.
- General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union agreed to set a target at the beginning of next week to resolve the union's strike.
- U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in September.
- Apple Computer Inc quarterly profit totalled $25 million, surprising stock market expectations.
- Ford Motor Co quarterly net income nearly doubled but most of the amount came from financial services.
- Higher air fares helped Continental Airlines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines gain strong quarterly profits.
- Merck and Co Inc, Johnson & Johnson and Schering-Plough Corp posted robust quarterly earnings.
- Compaq Computer Corp's quarterly profit soared 43 percent, reflecting stronger sales.
- BankAmerica Corp, Fleet Financial Group Inc and Wachovia Corp met or surpassed analysts' expectations for their quarterly results.
- Sears, Roebuck and Co reported a 22-percent increase in quarterly profit.
- Computer Associates International Inc saw its stock price fall 4.4 percent as it reported lower overseas software sales.
- The head of the Philadelphia Stock Exchange stepped down under pressure over his links with an exchange supplier.
- Dow Jones industrial average closed 16.03 points higher to a record 6,020.81, while U.S. bond prices recovered lost ground but still ended down.

- Short-term bond issues reacted to news of a stable U.S. consumer price inflation, while long-term ones ended moderately lower as traders foresaw higher inflation for the upcoming, fourth-quarter holiday season.
- Money managers are having a good year as the stocks they picked are up an average 14.7 percent throughout September 30.
